items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: John Sincero was living up in Chicago, I think, and I used to copy some of his stuff.

ctx.x: When you were coming up, you know like when you first started playing banjo, your idol was John Marrero. That's right.

One of them, I always met John Marrero, but John Sincero was living up in Chicago, I think, and I used to copy some of his stuff. And I actually copied some of Les Paul, the other guy who used to be with, Benny Goodman, a black fellow, he died. He's all a Christian. He's a great way. You have to do that to keep yourself voices down, you see.
What did you like about Marrero? I mean you took over, I mean you saw him quite a bit, I gather, down here. What about his playing did you like? I've never saw him.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Because Johnny, not only Johnny's sincere, there was a couple of other guys around there.

ctx.x: What about banjo, how did they tune them in the old days? Everybody used a four string tenor or a spectrum or five string?

Well I can tell you about that. When the banjo, now when they had banjos in the band like I said, they were using the guitar banjo. Because Johnny, not only Johnny's sincere, there was a couple of other guys around there. A fellow named Lorenzo Starr. They used a banjo guitar. In fact like I said before I started playing professional in 24, before the banjo got popular, that's what they were using. And that thing had a pretty good carrying power. Because I remember there was a guy with Sam Morgan band, that was…
